text:
Abstract
We assessed whether GEO Series GSE309890 provides raw sequencing reads suitable for assembly. Using GEO (Series record), NCBI SRA (runs-for-project), and ENA (study filereport), we retrieved study metadata and raw-read availability, focusing on organism, assay type, and download links. GSE309890 is an Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 RNA-seq study with 6 samples (Series entry, FTP directory shows processed FPKM counts only). The linked BioProject PRJNA1363958 has 6 SRA runs, all Illumina HiSeq 4000, paired-end RNA-Seq (transcriptomic) libraries. ENA lists fastq HTTPS download URLs for all 6 runs. Because all runs are RNA-Seq, genome assembly is not appropriate; transcriptome assembly or mapping-based expression analysis are feasible. Key numbers: 6 samples in GEO; 6 SRA/ENA runs; library strategy RNA-Seq for all; organism taxid 511145. This matters because GEO often hosts processed matrices while raw reads reside in SRA/ENA; distinguishing RNA-Seq versus WGS determines whether a genome assembly can be run. Our result provides direct fastq links and clarifies that assembly of the E. coli genome is unsupported for this dataset, while transcriptome analyses are suitable.

I. Introduction
Background. GSE309890 investigates SSRI-induced resistance dynamics in Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 via RNA-seq expression profiling (Series metadata). The user asked whether raw reads are available and if an assembly can be run.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. It was unclear whether the GEO Series contained raw reads versus only processed matrices, and whether the associated raw data were whole-genome sequencing (WGS) suitable for genome assembly.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Determine the availability and type of raw reads for GSE309890 and whether they support genome assembly. Hypothesis: The linked raw reads are RNA-Seq, available via SRA/ENA, and not appropriate for genome assembly.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We queried GEO to confirm Series-level metadata and supplementary files, then used SRA to enumerate runs in the linked BioProject, and ENA to obtain fastq download links. This chain addresses GEO→SRA/ENA provenance for raw data.
Materials.
- GEO Series via functions.geo_series.
- NCBI SRA via functions.ncbi_sra_runs_for_project.
- ENA study filereport via functions.brc_ena_study.
Procedures.
- functions.geo_series with arguments: {"accession":"GSE309890","list_files":true}.
- functions.ncbi_sra_runs_for_project with arguments: {"accession":"PRJNA1363958","max_results":200}.
- functions.brc_ena_study with arguments: {"study_accession":"PRJNA1363958"}.
Statistical Analysis.
- Sample count (6) taken from GEO Series field record.sample_count.
- Run count (6) taken from SRA result_count and ENA run_count fields; both agree.
- Library strategy, layout, taxon, and instrument model taken per-run from SRA and ENA fields; no deduplication required since the study lists 6 distinct SRR accessions.
- Download links from ENA fastq_https fields are reported per run; no percentages computed.

III. Results
Data Presentation. Table 1 lists the raw-read runs and fastq URLs from ENA.

Table 1. Raw RNA-seq runs and download links for PRJNA1363958 (GSE309890-associated study)
| Run accession | Sample title | Library strategy | Layout | Read count | Fastq_1 HTTPS | Fastq_2 HTTPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| SRR36018641 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep2 | RNA-Seq | Paired | 11997182 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_2.fastq.gz |
| SRR36018642 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep1 | RNA-Seq | Paired | 11992461 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_2.fastq.gz |
| SRR36018643 | E. coli, control,rep3 | RNA-Seq | Paired | 11720219 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_2.fastq.gz |
| SRR36018644 | E. coli, control,rep2 | RNA-Seq | Paired | 10415434 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_2.fastq.gz |
| SRR36018645 | E. coli, control,rep1 | RNA-Seq | Paired | 11621726 | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_1.fastq.gz | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_2.fastq.gz |

Findings.
- GEO Series GSE309890 lists 6 samples and provides processed expression values (FPKMs) via one CSV supplementary file; no raw reads in GEO.
- The linked BioProject PRJNA1363958 has 6 SRA runs; all are Illumina HiSeq 4000 paired-end RNA-Seq with taxid 511145 (E. coli K-12 MG1655).
- ENA provides fastq HTTPS links for all 6 runs.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation.
- Raw reads are available for GSE309890 via its linked SRA/ENA study PRJNA1363958. They are RNA-Seq reads suitable for expression profiling and, if desired, de novo transcriptome assembly or reference-based mapping. Genome assembly is not supported by these RNA-Seq libraries.
Context.
- GEO hosts processed matrices only for this Series (FPKMs), consistent with Series metadata and supplementary files. The raw data reside in SRA/ENA, as shown by the 6 paired-end RNA-Seq runs and their fastq links.
Limitations.
- GEO lacks a PubMed link; the study may be unpublished or not indexed yet. ENA metadata show missing collection dates. SRA download paths include lite SRA objects, but ENA fastq HTTPS links are provided and typically preferred for direct read retrieval.
Conclusion & Future Directions.
- You can obtain raw reads from ENA for all 6 runs using the fastq HTTPS links in Table 1. These reads support transcriptome analyses, not genome assembly. If genome assembly is desired, the next query worth running is an ENA search for whole-genome sequencing (WGS) runs for Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 or for a specific BioProject that includes WGS.

Findings.
- GEO Series GSE309890 lists 6 samples and provides processed expression values (FPKMs) via one CSV supplementary file; no raw reads in GEO.
- The linked BioProject PRJNA1363958 has 6 SRA runs; all are Illumina HiSeq 4000 paired-end RNA-Seq with taxid 511145 (E. coli K-12 MG1655).
- ENA provides fastq HTTPS links for all 6 runs.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation.
- Raw reads are available for GSE309890 via its linked SRA/ENA study PRJNA1363958. They are RNA-Seq reads suitable for expression profiling and, if desired, de novo transcriptome assembly or reference-based mapping. Genome assembly is not supported by these RNA-Seq libraries.
Context.
- GEO hosts processed matrices only for this Series (FPKMs), consistent with Series metadata and supplementary files. The raw data reside in SRA/ENA, as shown by the 6 paired-end RNA-Seq runs and their fastq links.
Limitations.
- GEO lacks a PubMed link; the study may be unpublished or not indexed yet. ENA metadata show missing collection dates. SRA download paths include lite SRA objects, but ENA fastq HTTPS links are provided and typically preferred for direct read retrieval.
Conclusion & Future Directions.
- You can obtain raw reads from ENA for all 6 runs using the fastq HTTPS links in Table 1. These reads support transcriptome analyses, not genome assembly. If genome assembly is desired, the next query worth running is an ENA search for whole-genome sequencing (WGS) runs for Escherichia coli K-12 MG1655 or for a specific BioProject that includes WGS.
